result.title: When the tail is earned by its companions: measuring label dependence in long-tailed multi-label classification
result.comment: 27 pages, 3 figures, 13 tables. Submitted to Information Sciences
result.summary: A rare label seldom occurs alone, and a classifier can recover it from the frequent labels it co-occurs with, its companions, without having learned the label itself. Existing diagnostics of this need a trained model: none says before training whether a corpus admits the failure, or what the standard aggregate hides. Macro-F1, like any measure built from per-label confusion counts, is unchanged by how a label's recall divides between occurrences with and without a companion. We introduce a within-label estimand of that division, a reading rule under which a fall in dependence counts only if companion-free recall rises, and a statistic of training labels that bounds, before training, how far reported recall can exceed companion-free recall. Across 23 corpora, 7 training objectives and five families of label-correlation mechanisms, companion-free recall falls short on all six corpora where the estimand is defined. Up to 18.4% of the tail true positives macro-F1 credits would vanish at the companion-free rate, within the training-label bound on every corpus. No long-tail objective reduces the dependence, but architecture moves it. Models whose tail score is computed from other labels' predictions are strongly dependent.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对长尾多标签分类，提出标签依赖的 within-label 估计量、一条只承认伴随性召回下降的判读规则，以及仅用训练标签即可在训练前给出召回上限的统计界，并在 23 个语料、7 种训练目标和 5 类标签相关机制上测量尾部标签被共现标签「代答」的程度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把报告指标拆成「依赖捷径所得」与「独立能力所得」的度量与事前上界思路，可能可供核查 LVR/VLM 中答案究竟由视觉证据还是语言先验等旁路支撑；该工作属单模态分类测量，迁移需自行验证。
